# Race podium study (generated by research.py; do not edit by hand)

**Question:** how well can division 1st-5th place times be predicted from earlier
editions of the same race, and are the 80% intervals honest?

## Data

- `data/division_panel.csv`: every finisher of 96 RunSignup races with a usable earlier edition (492 race-distance-years as targets; 3900 division series), downloaded with all result pages (`download_runsignup.download_full_results`). The v0.7 study used only the top 150 finishers per edition, which truncated division sizes and dropped most age brackets of large races.
- Divisions: M/F open plus 5-year brackets 15-19 ... 70-74 and 75+. Cleaning: finishes faster than 3:50/mile, duplicate rows, editions with < 30 finishers, and result lists filed under two distances are dropped; years with two events of one distance are skipped.
- Cases: 7202 division-years with >= 1 earlier edition and >= 5 finishers in the target year (so places 1-5 exist).

## Protocol

- Walk-forward: a case uses only earlier editions of the same race/distance/division (and, for the cross-division prior, earlier editions of the same race's gender-open division).
- The target edition's field size is not used: the model assumes the recency-weighted mean of earlier division sizes (v0.7: plain mean). Results with the actual size (a hindsight input, like knowing registrations) are shown separately.
- Parameters are refitted for each test year Y in 2022-2026 on cases with target year < Y only (expanding window) and scored on year Y. Point parameters minimise mean |log error| of 1st place; the two sigma parameters minimise the 80% interval score (Gneiting & Raftery 2007) of places 1-5 and are then rescaled together so that 80% of the training residuals fall inside their intervals. Benchmarks have no fitted parameters.
- **Out-of-sample test set: 5741 division-years from 397 independent race editions (96 races).** Divisions of one race edition share weather, course and timing, so the race-edition count is the honest sample size.

## Results (out of sample, test years pooled)

| model | 1st MAE (s) | 1st MAPE | 1st median APE | 1st bias (s) | places 1-5 MAE (s) | 80% cov. 1st | 80% cov. 1-5 | 80% half-width | interval score |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| last edition (lag 1) | 239.0 | 12.44% | 8.17% | +49.7 | 327.3 | — | — | — | — |
| mean of earlier editions | 243.7 | 13.57% | 8.37% | +85.0 | 326.6 | — | — | — | — |
| v0.7 model | 230.9 | 12.71% | 8.19% | +72.3 | 316.6 | 59.8% | 56.2% | ±12.5% | 62.4 |
| v0.8 without cross-division prior | 202.6 | 10.44% | 7.57% | +22.3 | 277.9 | 79.6% | 77.7% | ±17.5% | 49.7 |
| v0.8 without field-size shift | 190.3 | 9.64% | 7.48% | -40.9 | 276.7 | 84.0% | 80.3% | ±18.3% | 48.1 |
| v0.8 without aging-in step | 188.2 | 9.52% | 7.39% | -21.4 | 262.5 | 82.6% | 79.3% | ±17.1% | 45.9 |
| **v0.8 model** | 186.4 | 9.41% | 7.32% | -26.6 | 262.3 | 83.1% | 79.4% | ±17.1% | 45.8 |

With the target's actual division size (hindsight): v0.7 model: MAPE 12.00%, 80% coverage 61.0%; v0.8 model: MAPE 9.17%, 80% coverage 81.0%.

- 1st-place MAPE: last edition 12.44%, mean of earlier editions 13.57%, v0.7 12.71%, v0.8 9.41% (30.7% lower than the mean benchmark).
- 80% interval coverage of 1st place: v0.7 59.8% -> v0.8 83.1% (places 1-5: 56.2% -> 79.4%). Lower interval score is better.
- Errors are heavy-tailed (tiny earlier divisions, course changes, mislabelled events): the median APE is far below the mean. MAE in seconds is dominated by long races; MAPE is the fairer cross-distance summary.

## Production defaults (refitted on all cases: in-sample)

- `time_spread` = 0.09, `recency_decay` = 0.7, `edition_weight_half_n` = 10, `prior_weight` = 0.5, `sigma_year_pct` = 5.18, `sigma_field_pct` = 2.47 (at N = 100).
- In-sample on all 7202 cases: MAPE 9.26%, 80% coverage 1st 84.1%, places 1-5 80.2%. `ballmonitor backtest race_podium` runs the model itself on the same cases (data/backtest.csv) and should reproduce these numbers.

## Caveats

- The target is the fastest division finisher. Award rules that move overall winners out of age groups are not scored (the backtest turns that step off).
- Races were sampled from RunSignup's search (US, mostly small and medium local races); results may not transfer to large championship races.
- Course changes, timing errors and mislabelled events are left in; they make the large-error tail.
- The age factor in the cross-division prior comes from `age_curves.py`, whose curves were fitted on the earlier top-150 RunSignup download (partly overlapping races), so the prior is not entirely independent of the test data.
